parsed.summary: The netlist implements the specified architecture: TPS2121 power mux, AP63203 3.3 V buck, ESP32-C3, three MAX31855 SPI thermocouple channels, TPS1H200 heater high-side switch, USB-C/12 V inputs, fan tach protection, and WS2812B status LED. Reference designators differ from the specification, but connectivity and component values match the intended design; no deviation that would materially change board behavior is supported by the files.

response.reasoning:
We need answer single JSON. Need analyze PCB design files vs spec. Need identify anomaly if any. Need systematic.

We have spec and netlist. Need compare. Spec describes intended design with references: U1 ESP32-C3-MINI-1, U2/U3/U4 MAX31855, U6 TPS1H200, U5 TPS2121, U8 AP63203. But netlist references differ: U8 ESP32, U5 TPS1H200, U11 TPS2121, U7 AP63203, thermocouples U4/U6/U9. This could be just renumbered references? Need judge if design files contain anomaly. The spec says netlist authoritative connectivity. Reference design may have different ref designators? It says source files. We need compare design intent not exact refs? But if components swapped? Need see values and connectivity.

Netlist components:
- U8 ESP32-C3-MINI-1 (MCU)
- U5 TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1 (heater switch)
- U11 TPS2121RUXR (power mux)
- U7 AP63203WU (buck)
- U4, U6, U9 MAX31855
- D4 WS2812B (status LED)
- D5 LED? In MCU sheet; spec says D1 WS2812B status LED. D5 LED maybe heater status? Spec D2 status LED on heater net. Netlist has D5 LED on net /Microcontroller/NET0004 with U5 IN/DIAG_EN and U8 GPIO1 and J1 pin2. That's heater control net? But D5 LED is on heater control GPIO net, not heater output. Spec says status LED D2 and R3 on HEATER net (heater output). Here D5 LED and R11? Let's inspect.

Power architecture:
Inputs:
J9 Barrel_Jack pin1 +12V, pin2 GND. Good.
J3 USB_C VBUS pins +5V to U11 IN2. Good.
CC1/CC2: J3 A5 CC1 -> Net-(J3-CC1) -> R5 pin2; R5 pin1 GND. R5 value 5.1k. CC2 -> R2 5.1k to GND. Good.

Mux U11:
IN1 pin7/7_1 +12V. IN2 pin2/2_1 +5V. OUT pins 1/1_1/8/8_1 -> VBUS. CP2 pin3, OV2 pin4, OV1 pin5, PR1 pin6, ST pin9 -> GND. ILIM pin10 -> R7 51.1k to GND. SS pin11 -> C19 10nF to GND. GND pin12. Matches spec (except refs U5 vs U11). VBUS net has C6 10uF, TP3, U7 EN/IN. Good.

Buck U7 AP63203:
IN pin3 VBUS, EN pin2 VBUS. SW pin5 -> Net-(U7-SW) with L2 pin1 and C17 pin1. BST pin6 -> Net-(U7-BST) with C17 pin2. FB pin1 -> +3V3. GND pin4. L2 pin2 +3V3. +3V3 net has C2 22uF, C20 22uF, C4 1uF, C18 1uF, C3 1uF, C5 1uF, C14 1uF, R10/R3/R6/R9 pin2, TP9, U4/U6/U9 Vcc, D4 VDD, U8 pin3. Matches spec (refs differ). Note spec says C13 bootstrap cap, but netlist C17. Fine.

Heater path:
Spec: U6 TPS1H200: VS pin8 +12V, IN/DIAG_EN pins1/2 GPIO1, OUT pin7 heater connector J6 pin2, CL pin4 GND, GND pin6 GND, EP pin9 GND, ~FAULT pin3 TP6. Status LED D2 and series R3 also on HEATER net. In netlist U5 TPS1H200:
- pin8 VS -> +12V net. Good.
- pin1 IN and pin2 DIAG_EN -> /Microcontroller/NET0004, also U8 pin13 GPIO1 and D5 pin2 A and J1 pin2. Wait J1 is Screw_Terminal_01x02 in Microcontroller sheet. Pin1 GND, pin2 NET0004. That means GPIO1/HEATER control net goes to a screw terminal? Spec says thermocouple J1 for U2? But here refs shifted: J1 in MCU sheet is a 2-pin screw terminal with pin1 GND pin2 heater control? That seems odd: a screw terminal connected to MCU GPIO1 and LED anode? Could be heater output? Let's inspect all connectors:
J1 Screw_Terminal_01x02 in Microcontroller sheet: pin1 GND, pin2 /Microcontroller/NET0004 (GPIO1 + U5 IN/DIAG_EN + D5 A). This looks like a terminal for heater control? But spec: J6 heater connector pin2 from U6 OUT. Netlist J6 in Thermocouples sheet: pin1 U4 T-, pin2 U4 T+ (thermocouple). J11/J12 in Thermocouples also thermocouple terminals. J4 in Microcontroller: pin1 GND, pin2 U5 OUT (heater output). So J4 is heater connector? Yes J4 pin2 Net-(J4-Pin_2) -> U5 pin7 OUT, pin1 GND. That matches heater connector (OUT to pin2, other pin GND). So J4 is heater output connector. J1 is something else? It is connected to GPIO1/IN/DIAG_EN/LED anode, pin1 GND. That could be a manual override? But spec says heater status LED D2 and series resistor R3 on HEATER net (OUT), not on GPIO control. In netlist, D5 LED anode pin2 to NET0004 (control net), cathode pin1 to Net-(D5-K) -> R11 500 to GND. So D5 is LED on GPIO1 control net to ground via 500Ω. That means LED lights when GPIO1 high? But GPIO1 also drives U5 IN/DIAG_EN high-side switch input. Is that intended? Spec says D2 status LED on HEATER net (output) with R3. But this build has D5 LED on control net with R11. Could be a different design? Need determine anomaly. But maybe D5 is the heater status LED? Wait spec says status LED D2 and series resistor R3 are also on the HEATER net, so heater output doubles as visual indicator. In netlist, R3 is 10k to +3V3 and D8-A net, not heater. R11 is 500 to D5-K. D5 is LED. This is not on heater output. But is that necessarily anomaly? It changes behavior: LED indicates MCU output rather than actual heater output; if high-side switch fails open, LED still on. But spec says intended D2 on HEATER net. However the netlist may have renumbered and maybe D5 is intended to be on HEATER? Let's trace: U5 IN/DIAG_EN is not HEATER output; OUT is J4 pin2. D5 is not on OUT. So deviation from spec. But could be acceptable? Need see if it makes board behave differently. It would light LED when MCU asserts heater, not when heater energized. But spec's known limitations? Not mention. Could be anomaly if deliberate tampering? Need compare all.

But bigger anomalies likely: U5 TPS1H200 IN and DIAG_EN connected to GPIO1 net that also includes J1 screw terminal and D5 LED. J1 pin1 GND, pin2 control. A screw terminal tied to GPIO1 and high-side switch input? Could be an external switch? If J1 is a connector, pin1 GND pin2 GPIO1. If someone connects a wire between J1 pins, pulls GPIO1 low? But GPIO1 is output driving heater; short to GND could fault MCU. But maybe J1 is intended as thermocouple? Wait spec says three thermocouple channels J1/J2/J3 screw terminals to MAX31855 T+/T-. In netlist, thermocouple terminals are J6/J11/J12? Let's map: U4, U6, U9 MAX31855. Their T-/T+ connect to J6, J11, J12. J1 is not thermocouple. J4 is heater. J2/J5 are fan headers. J3 USB, J9 barrel. So J1 is extra screw terminal connected to GPIO1/switch input. Spec doesn't mention any screw terminal on GPIO1. Could be anomaly: extra connector or miswired LED? Need evaluate.

Also fan tach inputs:
Spec: 2 fan tachometers with TVS-diode-protected inputs. Netlist: J2 and J5 fan pin headers. J2 pin1 GND, pin2 +12V, pin3 NET0010, pin4 no_connect. NET0010: D7 pin1 A1, D8 pin3 K, J2 pin3. D7 is D_TVS bidirectional? pins A1/A2; pin2 A2 GND. D8 is diode; pin1 A -> Net-(D8-A), pin3 K -> NET0010. Net-(D8-A): R3 10k to +3V3, TP2, U8 GPIO21/U0TXD. So fan tach input from J2 pin3 goes to D8 cathode? Let's understand: J2 pin3 to D8 K (pin3), D8 A to GPIO21. D7 TVS from J2 pin3 to GND. This is a pull-up resistor R3 to +3V3, diode D8? Usually fan tach is open collector; pull-up to 3.3V, signal to GPIO. TVS to GND. But diode D8 orientation: pin1 A to GPIO, pin3 K to fan. If fan pin pulls low, current from GPIO? Wait open-collector fan: tach pin internal NPN to GND, needs pull-up to voltage. If pull-up is on signal node (fan side), then GPIO sees high when fan not pulling low. Here pull-up R3 is on D8 anode/GPIO side, not fan side. D8 cathode to fan. If GPIO is input high-Z, R3 pulls anode high, but diode blocks to fan? Fan node has no pull-up except via TVS? If fan open collector, fan node floats low? Actually fan tach output is open drain to GND when spinning pulses; when high it is high impedance. Without pull-up on fan node, fan node floats, diode cathode floats; GPIO sees R3 pull-up through diode? If diode anode pulled high, cathode maybe can be pulled low by fan? But diode only conducts from anode to cathode (A to K). If fan pulls cathode low, diode conducts from GPIO/R3 to fan, clamping GPIO? That seems wrong: pull-up should be on fan node, diode maybe for ESD? Let's inspect spec: "Monitors 2 fan tachometers with TVS-diode-protected inputs". The netlist has TVS D7/D9 and diodes D8/D6. D8/D6 orientation? libpart D: pin1 A, pin3 K. D8 pin3 K to fan, pin1 A to GPIO. D6 pin3 K to fan J5 pin3, pin1 A to GPIO20. So diode anode to GPIO, cathode to fan. This is reverse of typical? Maybe they use diode to protect GPIO from fan voltage? If fan pulls up? Let's analyze: If fan tach output is open collector, the fan side should be pulled up to 3.3V via R3/R10. But here pull-ups are on GPIO side. When fan pulls low, it pulls diode cathode low; diode anode (GPIO) high through R3 -> diode forward biases, current flows from R3/GPIO into fan low, pulling GPIO down? Actually GPIO input high impedance, R3 pulls anode to 3.3V, diode anode 3.3V, cathode fan pulled 0V => diode forward, anode clamped ~0.7V, so GPIO sees low. When fan high impedance, cathode floats; diode may not conduct; anode pulled 3.3V, GPIO high. So it works as a diode clamp: pull-up on GPIO side, fan low pulls through diode. But current flows from R3 to fan, okay. The fan sees current? Open collector can sink. This is acceptable maybe. TVS on fan side to GND. Good.

But D5 LED on control net: R11 500 to GND. GPIO1 high -> LED current 3.3V-2V/500 ~2.6mA, okay. But GPIO1 also drives TPS1H200 IN/DIAG_EN. Input current small. Fine. But J1 screw terminal on same net: if used as output? Could be an external indicator or switch? Not in spec.

Need check SPI:
NET0002 SO: U4 pin7, U6 pin7, U9 pin7, U8 pin16 GPIO10. Good.
NET0008 SCK: U4/U6/U9 pin5, U8 pin19 GPIO5. Good.
CS: U9 pin6 -> GPIO4 NET0011; U6 pin6 -> GPIO7 NET0019; U4 pin6 -> GPIO6 NET0003. Spec says CS0 GPIO4, CS1 GPIO6, CS2 GPIO7. Mapping okay. NC pin8 unconnected for all. Good.

That's reverse-biased under normal positive 12V, conducts on negative. Spec says D7 plain diode reverse polarity protection. Here D11 is plain diode, orientation same: cathode to +12V, anode GND. Good. But spec says commit title TVS mismatch; not anomaly. However netlist D11 footprint D_SMA, value D. Good.

But note: +12V net has C15 0.1uF and C8 10uF. Spec says C1 bulk caps C1/C2. okay.

But spec says R11? Netlist R11 500 LED series. Fine.
